THE SECOND REVIEW OF 1.24.34 (a lift station's schematic and the drawings it needs), at 39a4fe2 (the draft with the
first review's mends), beside 1.24.33 as released (0dfc9d8). Written by a reviewer that wrote none of the change and
read the first review (../liftstation_review1_1234/findings.txt) only after every case here was written.

HOW TO REPLAY
  node tests/fixtures/liftstation_review2_1234/replay.js [lantern.inner.html] [--only <id regex>]     (jsdom, ~3 s)
  python3 tests/fixtures/liftstation_review2_1234/replay_browser.py <out dir>     (Chromium; draws render_inputs.js)
  run_39a4fe2.txt is the run this file reports. load.js is a copy of ../liftstation_review1_1230/load.js; lib.js loads
  the draft and 1.24.33 (git show 0dfc9d8 into the temp folder). Each case {id, harm, input, right, run}: run() is ""
  when Lantern does right. Harm: high = a wrong thing drawn, accepted or said as right, or a line handed to the model
  that makes a wrong circuit; medium = a wrong line handed back, a wrong thing said beside a right drawing, a block
  shown twice, the one drawing asked for buried in three; low = wording, names, rare inputs.

WHAT WAS RUN, AND WHAT WAS NOT
  Run: 249 cases in jsdom with a scripted model (whole Chat turns through L.CHAT.turn; the bench's path through
  aiAct.solve and aiBench.grade). The bench guard: all 300 questions of aiBenchQuestions and aiBenchQuestionsB, and all
  562 replies and first replies saved in tests/fixtures/bench_run*.json built on both versions: identical.
  tests/liftstation_1234.js passes (29). Eleven results drawn in Chromium (replay_browser.py) and looked at: the 35B's
  station (Adam's question) and its piping block alone; the triplex with "Pump 3 On"; "Start"/"Start 2"; "Lag On /
  High Alarm"; a relay contact "High Level"; a schematic then MAKE STATION; British piping; and three circuits with
  Lantern's line written in (the short, a named terminal, the 35B's second try). PNGs were written to the session's
  scratchpad, not kept here.
  Not run: no real model (every reply here is this reviewer's); npm test; the bench on GitHub.

COUNTS
  A which tool (routing; the bench guard)     87 cases, 20 DISAGREE (3 high, 9 medium, 8 low)
  B part-and-wire blocks read as the station   53 cases, 17 DISAGREE (4 high, 8 medium, 5 low)
  C what a float is for (floatJob, key, lags)  58 cases, 14 DISAGREE (0 high, 7 medium, 7 low)
  D the open circuit's line                    23 cases,  8 DISAGREE (3 high, 3 medium, 2 low)
  E Chat's other blocks; rec.made; solve       19 cases,  6 DISAGREE (1 high, 2 medium, 3 low)
  F view(): the advice and the header           9 cases,  0 DISAGREE
  In all: 249 cases: 184 AGREE, 65 DISAGREE (11 high, 29 medium, 25 low).

WHAT HOLDS
  - The bench: every question keeps its tools, every saved reply builds as on 1.24.33 (A-bench-*); rec.made, the
    calls and act.solve are as on 1.24.33 for multi-block replies (E-rec-made-unchanged, E-solve-unchanged); Adam's
    question on the bench's path passes make-liftstation's checks (E-solve-adam-bench).
  - Adam's question and 28 other ways of asking for a station's drawings with write/give/produce/prepare/provide/
    generate/draft/put together go to MAKE STATION; 33 documents, questions in words, programs, devices and other
    stations do not (A-*).
  - The 35B's two blocks make the station: H2 off, H1 lead (said), H3 alarm, each pump a check valve then a gate valve,
    the vent, inlet and force main. Seen in Chromium: the floats in that order, the valves in that order on each pump.
  - Most right part-and-wire blocks read right: classic duplex with a horn, unquoted names, switches named float,
    "Pump 1 Start"/"Pump 2 Start", PA/PB pumps, a fan motor left out, six floats (low level alarm, redundant off, off,
    lead, lag, two alarms), the low water cutoff under the off, the e-stop and reset switches left out, push buttons
    left out, simplex sumps (one float, an unnamed motor, high/low), lowercase bullets, a triplex's "Lag 1"/"Lag 2",
    ISA LSLL/LSL/LSH/LSHH with names, plug valves with the inlet and force main, swing checks, two kinds of shutoff
    valve, the dry well left out and said, a holding tank left out, 2 and 3 pumps said, MAKE CONTROL or MAKE PIPING
    beside a part-and-wire block, panel-light and HOA-only blocks not read as stations.
  - "Emergency high" and its spellings are the alarm; emergency off/stop/low/cutoff/shutdown are off; "start both
    pumps"/"lag start" lag; low water cutoff, shutdown, shutoff off (C-*). MAKE LEVELS takes a triplex's two lag
    floats and a four-pump station's three, and refuses two for a duplex.
  - The plain lines are right: a dead end, one ground, parallel lamps to ground, a diode, an RC, a source; no line
    where the ground is midway, two ends, two grounds, the battery wired only to ground (D-*).
  - Chat: a circuit and a table, two circuits, a drawing and a program each shown; a table held across a correction
    (and across a correction in prose) shown once; "Make sure:"/"Make note:" not blocks; the station's own example
    after its block not made (E-*). view(): the advice is the action's, "Ask again." for empty ones, the header names
    a pump station and what could not be made (F-*).

FINDINGS, MOST HARM FIRST

1. HIGH. A float the AI wrote is dropped from every drawing while the summary says it was taken, and what is then said
   is untrue (B-duplex-start-start2, B-triplex-pump3on, B-probes-stop-start-high high; B-duplex-pump1off-pump2off
   medium; their roots C-start-2, C-pump-3-on, C-start-pump-3 medium).
   floatJob reads "Start 2", "Pump 3 On", "Start Pump 3" as lead (only "pump 2"/"second"/"2nd" are lag), and spec()
   merges a float whose key another float already has as "the same float said twice" even when each has its own tag
   from the schematic. That merge was made for a floats line and a float line of one float, one of them untagged.
   - "Stop", "Start", "Start 2", "Alarm": drawn F1, F2, F4. The summary lists F3 "Start 2" among the floats it took,
     then says "no lag float in the AI's schematic: one pump runs at a time". Seen in Chromium: the control has no lag
     call, and its note says the same.
   - Triplex "Pumps Off", "Pump 1 On", "Pump 2 On", "Pump 3 On", "High Level Alarm": the levels drawing (Chromium) has
     F1, F2, F3, F5. F4 is listed as taken; the third pump has no float to start it, and nothing says so.
   - Probes E1 "Stop", E2 "Start", E3 "High": E3 merged into E2, then "no high level alarm float: the block has none".
   - "Pump 1 Off", "Pump 2 Off": F2 listed, not drawn.
   Expected: two tagged floats are two floats. A second float of the same job is the next job up, as floatList already
   does for "pump 2 on": a second start is the lag, a third pump's start a second lag on a triplex. Or it is said "not
   drawn". The floats the summary names are the ones drawn.

2. HIGH. The ground line closes a dead short, and Lantern then accepts it (D-short-through-switch,
   D-short-through-junction, D-lamp-bypassed).
   B1 to S1, S1 to G1, and L1 on S1 alone (the model meant S1 to L1 to G1): Lantern hands "L1 is on one wire too: say
   where it goes on; join the ground back to B1, like: wire G1 B1". Written, the circuit is made as "4 parts, 4
   connections, a closed loop": the battery shorted through the switch, the lamp hanging. Through a junction (B1 to J1
   to G1) it is a short with no part at all. Seen in Chromium: B1 to S1 to a wire straight back to B1's other side,
   L1 off the end. Lantern's own short check does not see it, because a two-terminal part on one wire (L1) makes
   AI_SCHEMATIC_CHECK's netlist() "unsure" and the check is skipped. Rule 7: the line makes the wrong circuit, and
   Lantern draws it as right.
   Expected: the ground line only where the way from the source to the ground passes a load (a lamp, motor, resistor
   ...), never through switches, junctions or wires alone. A two-terminal part still on one wire after a line is
   questioned.
   Related, MEDIUM: D-junction-end. B1 to S1 to J1: "like: wire J1 B1" shorts the battery through S1. Written, it is
   caught as a short, but only after the one correction has been spent.

3. HIGH. MAKE STATION written after a part-and-wire schematic is dropped, and Chat says something untrue about it
   (B-schematic-then-station, E-schematic-then-station high; E-station-then-schematic medium; E-station-then-control
   low).
   A reply with the schematic first and then "MAKE STATION: Lift station / pumps 3 / floats ... / well "wet well"
   12 ft": build() takes the first block, so the station is drawn from the schematic (2 pumps, no well depth).
   MAKE STATION's lines, the block the instructions asked for, are not read. rest() skips it with "The AI also wrote
   MAKE STATION: Lift station beside the station; the station's drawings are made from its one block, so it was not
   made again." That is untrue: that block was never made, and the station came from another block.
   The other way round (MAKE STATION pumps 3, then an electrical schematic of 2 pumps, or a MAKE CONTROL with a lag
   float and a horn the station lacks), the same note says the block "was not made again". It was never made or read,
   and the disagreement is not said.
   Expected: a MAKE STATION block in the reply is the station, whichever comes first. Blocks beside it that are not
   read are said to be not read, with any disagreement (pumps 2 against 3).

4. HIGH. The station before the drawing word still gets the hobby-part MAKE SCHEMATIC, which is Adam's failure again
   (A-miss-lift-station-schematic, A-miss-give-lift-station-schematic, A-miss-duplex-lift-station-schematic high;
   A-miss-do-a-schematic, A-miss-do-up, A-miss-do-the-drawings, A-miss-will-you, A-miss-would-you-write-up,
   A-miss-give-lift-station-drawings medium; A-miss-i-need, A-miss-hyphen, A-miss-list-and-draw low).
   "Write a lift station schematic", "Give me a lift station schematic" and "Write a duplex lift station schematic"
   are offered MAKE SCHEMATIC, whose prompt is battery, source, resistor ... lamp, motor. That is the prompt that
   failed in Adam's chat. WHOLE_W needs the drawing word before the station, so it misses the most natural English
   order. ("Draw a lift station schematic" is MAKE STATION, through WHOLE.)
   "do" is one of WHOLE_W's verbs, but the new words-opener rejects a question that begins with "do" before WHOLE_W
   is tried. So "Do a schematic for a lift station" and "Do up a schematic of a duplex lift station" get MAKE
   SCHEMATIC, and "Do the drawings for our sewage lift station" gets MAKE DRAWING (the grid picture).
   "Will you write a schematic for a lift station?" gets MAKE SCHEMATIC ("will" was added to the opener), while
   "Could you ..." and "Can you ..." get MAKE STATION. "Would you write up the drawings for a lift station?" and
   "Give me lift station drawings" get the grid picture.
   All of these behaved the same way on 1.24.33, but the change was made to fix this failure.
   Expected: write/give/do ... a <station> schematic/drawings is the station's, whichever word comes first. The opener
   catches "do/does/will ..." only as a question ("Do you/I/we ...", "Does ...", "Will it ..."), not as "Do a
   schematic ..." or "Will you write ...".

5. MEDIUM. Asking for one drawing and saying the others are not wanted still gets all three (A-one-do-not-include,
   A-one-already-have, A-one-others-done medium; A-one-as-drawings-require low).
   "Draw the control circuit for a lift station; do not include any other drawings", "Draw just the control circuit
   for the lift station, I already have the other drawings." and "Draw the float levels for the lift station; the
   other drawings are already done": allDrawn() finds "any other drawings" / "the other drawings" with "draw" or
   "include" before it in the sentence. These go to MAKE STATION, and spec() draws all three. On 1.24.33 they went to
   the one drawing asked for. "... as the city's drawings require" is caught the same way, through "drawings ...
   require".
   Expected: ALLDRAW never counts after a negation (not, no, don't, without, already have, already done) or as the
   subject of "are done/require". Then the one drawing asked for is drawn alone.

6. MEDIUM. A part that is not a float is read as a float, or sent back to be named one (B-relay-contact-not-float,
   B-limit-switch-not-float, B-limit-switch-type, B-isa-tags-no-names medium; B-back-quotes-the-models-line low).
   - A relay contact CR1 "High Level" (a contact type, PT_SENSE) is drawn as a second high level alarm float. Seen in
     Chromium: "CR1 High Level" hangs in the wet well above F3.
   - LS is the limit switch's tag on a NEMA/JIC ladder. 'part LS2 switch "Limit Switch"' and "part LS1 limit switch"
     (the type says limit) are read as floats by FTAG. The whole station goes back with 'name its job, like: float LS2
     "high level alarm"'. Rule 7: that line turns a limit switch into an alarm float.
   - ISA tags with no names (LSL1, LSH1, LSHH1): the tags say what each float does, but the lines handed back are
     LSL1 "off", LSH1 "lead on" and LSHH1 "lag on". High-high is the alarm, and the line goes against the model's
     own tag.
   - What goes back quotes "float LS1 “Level Switch 1”", a line Lantern made from "part LS1 switch ...". The model
     never wrote it.
   Expected: a contact, relay or limit switch type is never a float. An FS/LS tag makes a switch a float only when
   nothing in its type or name says limit. ISA suffixes (L, LL, H, HH) give the job. The problem quotes the model's
   own line.

7. MEDIUM. "Lag On / High Alarm": the summary contradicts the circuit Lantern draws (B-duplex-lag-and-alarm-one-float).
   AI_STATION's spec reads F3 as the alarm. AI_PUMP_STATION's levels turns alarm+lag into lag, but AI_STATION does
   not. The control circuit it draws (seen in Chromium) runs both pumps on F3 through CR2 and lights the alarm. The
   levels drawing shows F3 as the lag float. Yet the summary, the description and the PDF all say "no lag float in the
   AI's schematic: one pump runs at a time (a lag float above the lead one would start the other too)". The checks
   have no "lift F3: both pumps run".
   Expected: a float named lag and alarm is the lag float in spec(), as in MAKE LEVELS and MAKE CONTROL. No "no lag
   float" note.

8. MEDIUM. The valve tags in Adam's own summary contradict his drawing (B-35b-valve-tags).
   "the check valves (V1, V2), the shutoff valves (V3, V4)" are the 35B's tags. The piping drawn labels CV1 and CV2 as
   the checks and V1 and V2 as the gate valves (Chromium: "V1 gate", "V2 gate"). The same summary also lists "V1
   (source)" as not carried (the electrical block's V1). A reader holding the drawing reads V1 as a check valve.
   Expected: each part named by the tag on the drawing, with the AI's tag beside it ("CV1, CV2 (the AI's V1, V2)"), and
   a tag reused across two blocks told apart by block.

9. MEDIUM. The dry well's sump pump makes a triplex (B-piping-dry-well-sump-pump).
   'part P3 pump "Dry Well Sump Pump"' beside two lift pumps is counted, so the station has 3 pumps and its control
   circuit is not drawn. Expected: a pump named for the dry well, seal water, a sampler, a bypass or a portable pump is
   not a lift pump (not carried, said).

10. MEDIUM. Triplex and duplex lag floats in MAKE STATION disagree with MAKE LEVELS (C-station-triplex-lag-on-twice,
    C-station-duplex-lag12, C-levels-triplex-three-lags-back).
    - MAKE STATION pumps 3 with two "lag on" floats at 4 ft and 5 ft goes back with "two heights for the lag on float
      (4 ft and 5 ft): write it once, like: float FS3 "lag on" 4 ft". That line deletes the second lag pump's float.
      MAKE LEVELS now draws this case, and its own line writes "lag on" twice.
    - A duplex with "lag 1 on" and "lag 2 on" (1.24.33 merged them and drew the station) now passes spec() (keys lag1,
      lag2) and is refused by the control and the levels drawings. Their lines repeat both lag floats: copied, they
      fix nothing.
    - MAKE LEVELS' line for three lag floats on a triplex repeats all three. This was already so on 1.24.33.
    Expected: spec() allows a lag float for each pump after the lead, as planLevels does, and refuses the rest with a
    line that has one fewer.

11. MEDIUM. With Lantern's line written, a circuit with parts on one wire is accepted without a word (D-island,
    D-35b-second-try medium; D-ground-and-loose-lamp low).
    The 35B's own second try, with "wire G1 V1" written as told, is made as "a closed loop" while the stop buttons
    S5 and S7 each sit on one wire. They stop nothing, and the line had named them only before it. Seen in Chromium:
    S5 is drawn in a row with M1 and S4, as if it were in series. Labels are drawn on top of each other ("M2 (Pump 2)"
    on "L2", "L3" on "S6"), and wires run off below the drawing.
    Two lamps wired only to each other (an island) are accepted the same way once the loop is closed. The cause is
    older than this change (no check questions a two-terminal part on one wire, and the netlist then skips the short
    check: see 2). The line now leads models there.

12. MEDIUM. Chat shows the same circuit twice (E-self-corrected-copy).
    A reply has an open circuit, then "Oops ... Corrected:" and the right one. Lantern asks again (the first block is
    built), shows the correction, then shows the held copy, the same circuit with the same title and lines. The held
    blocks are filtered by kind against the corrected reply's own other blocks only.
    Expected: a held block identical to the made one (sameBlock) is not shown again.

13. MEDIUM (older than this change, in reach of it). C-emergency-redundant-start: "Emergency High (Redundant Start)"
    is read as off ("redundant" wins), so a start float is wired to stop the pumps. "Emergency High / All Pumps On" is
    lead, not lag (low).

14. LOW. Over-reach of WHOLE_W on writing about a drawing (A-no-legend, A-no-explanation, A-no-symbols, A-no-notes).
    "Write a schematic legend for a lift station", "Give me a schematic explanation of a lift station", "Give me the
    schematic symbols used on lift station drawings" and "Write the schematic notes for the lift station" are MAKE
    STATION (on 1.24.33, MAKE SCHEMATIC). Expected: legend, explanation, symbols and notes join DRAWOBJ's negative
    lookahead.

15. LOW. AI_PUMP_STATION's fallback floatJob is not "the same rule" (C-fallback-shutdown, C-fallback-pump-shutdown:
    the draft added shutdown/cutoff to AI_CONTROL only; C-fallback-both-run, C-fallback-lag-off: older). It reads
    "Emergency Shutdown" and "Pump Shutdown" as nothing, "emergency high level both pumps run" as the alarm, and "Lag
    Off" as lag, where AI_CONTROL reads off, off, lag and off. It matters only with AI_CONTROL dropped.

16. LOW. Prose that begins "Make <a kind>:" is shown as a failed block under a right answer (E-prose-make-kind,
    E-prose-make-sheet). "**Make Drawing:** if you want a picture, ask me." and "Make Sheet: optional, if you want ..."
    show "Lantern could not make a drawing: ** if you want a picture ...". Expected: a block with no line of its
    action's grammar, or a title that is a sentence, is not built by rest().

17. LOW. Smaller things said wrong (B-piping-british, B-piping-valve-pit, B-duplex-motor-labels, B-title-keeps-name;
    C-emergency-cut-out, C-pump-cut-out; D-port-short-unseen).
    - A British "Sluice Valve" on a pump's discharge is its gate valve. It is said not carried, and the drawing shows
      shutoff valves with no kind.
    - A "Valve Pit" is called the wet well (VP1).
    - Two motors "Motor 1" and "Motor 2" beside lead and lag floats are "not carried (motor)" with "2 pumps: the block
      did not say".
    - "Electrical Schematic - Main Street Lift Station" is named "Pump station".
    - "Cut Out" (with a space) is no job.
    - "wire B1+ S1, wire S1 B1" is a short that is not caught: the netlist puts B1+ and an unnamed second wire on one
      terminal. This is older; Lantern's line writes exactly that mix after a named terminal, though the drawing
      itself (Chromium) put G1 on the battery's other side, rightly.

OBSERVATIONS WITHOUT A CASE
  - ASSIST_CHAT uses rec.more for two things. Line ~21646 (1.24.18) sets it to the library's extra titles (strings).
    The draft pushes made results into it, and line ~21655 reorders the passages for libraryPointer whenever rec.more
    is set. I could not drive both in one turn with a scripted model. A field of its own (rec.moreMade) would remove
    the doubt.
  - In Chromium, older text: the levels drawing of Adam's station says "(float FS2 "lead on" 3.5 ft)" where its lead
    float is H1, and the control's note proposes "float FS1 "lag on"" (FS1 is conventionally the lowest float). Not
    from this change.

QUESTIONS FOR ADAM (judgement, not code)
  - Finding 4: should "write/give me a lift station schematic" (station before the drawing word) be MAKE STATION, as
    "draw a lift station schematic" is?
  - Finding 6: on a lift station's ladder, is LS1 more often a level switch or a limit switch in the drawings you see?
  - Finding 1: a sump/duplex with electrode probes "Stop/Start/High": is the High probe the alarm or the lag start in
    your practice?
